name: Candidati

abilities.name: Unbreakable
abilities.text: The unit's morale cannot be broken for an extended period of time.

abilities.name: Loyalty of the 10th
abilities.text: Target friendly units to greatly improve their defensive capabilities and make their morale unbreakable for an extended period. Can only be used once per battle.

abilities.name: Trample
abilities.text: Charges are more effective for an extended time.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

attributes.name: Scare (everyone)
attributes.text: This unit frightens all enemy units.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

short: Candidati - the Emperor's personal guard, where only the best men, selected from the Scholae Palatinae, were assigned. It is possible that already under Constantine, candidates (candidati) were chosen from the scholae, which formed the Emperor's personal protection. The name candidati comes from the white color of the clothes worn by the new bodyguards. In the Easter Chronicle it is said that «Gordian Augustus established a cohort of candidati, selecting from his legion the strongest and the most blooming age, and those who were strong and had an impressive body, who were called scholarians; and this unit of schola itself he called by his name the Elders; they were from the sixth schola». And further: «The Emperor Philip, together with his son Philip, established a cohort of the candidati, into which he took chosen young men from the scholarians, giving the title of Younger to the scholae of the legion which they had established, after the name of Philip's father; and they were also of the seventh schola». Apparently, one of the last candidati was Theophylact, executed in 765 AD by Constantine V on charges of malevolence (Theophanes dates this event to 757 AD).
history: Understandably, the protection of the Emperor was of the utmost importance. Only the most seasoned of troops were chosen to join the Emperor's personal guard, in a ceremony that involved the wearing of his priceless purple robes. To be a 'domestici', whilst a prestigious position in itself, was seen as the path to further accolades; after several years service, the Emperor usually granted you command of a military regiment. As time went by, the role took on civil functions as well as military ones. The works of Ammianus Marcellinus, who served as a domestici, are extensive primary sources for late antiquity; he chronicled most of Roman history from AD96 until the time of Constantine the Great.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
